newsitem.title: POLAND: HACHETTE PROTESTS AGAINST POLISH RUCH SALE SNAG.
newsitem.headline: HACHETTE PROTESTS AGAINST POLISH RUCH SALE SNAG.

text.p: Hachette Distribution Services on Tuesday threatened unspecified action against the Polish government if it broke a deal on selling newsstand chain Ruch SA to a consortium led by the French firm.
It said in a statement that the action would be taken if the treasury ministry agreed to consider a late bid for Ruch by a group of Polish companies led by trader Universal .

"If information regarding the offer...proves true and if the offer, which may lead to the annulment of the Ruch sale tender, is taken into account...the consortium will take all steps necessary to protect its interests," Hachette said.
In December last year, the ministry signed a initial agreement on selling Ruch to the Hachette-led consortium but later said it could consider a bid from another company if it proved better.
On Monday a consortium grouping Universal, private television Polsat SA and soft drink producer and publisher Multico SA, offered to pay $80 million for a 40-percent stake in Ruch.
The group also pledged to invest a total of $200 million in the company, which owns 17,000 kiosks nationwide and controls 65 percent of Poland's press distribution market.
Hachette officials were not immediately available to give details on what steps would be taken.
The treasury ministry distanced itself from the agreement with Hachette after the French firm revealed the agreed price to be paid for Ruch ahead of signing the final accord.

The daily Nowa Europa quoted Hachette's president Jean-Louis Nachury as saying his company would pay $84 million for a 75 percent stake in Ruch and then earmark a further $45 million for increasing its capital.
After the report, deputy treasury minister Leszek Juchniewicz said the agreement with Hachette was only tentative and that the ministry was seeking better terms for the sale.
The sale of Ruch, which netted 16.2 million zlotys on sales of 2.7 billion zlotys in 1995, to Hachette was strongly advocated by French President Jacques Chirac during his visit to Poland last year.
